Our story

The Olive Tree House was built by Lamprini's father, Dimitris, on land he had inherited from his own father, Theodoros.

Theodoros was a proud patriot. He fought against the Italians in Albania in 1940 and, when he returned to the village, he raised his family near the Church of Agia Thekli. He purchased the plot from the church — at the time, a vast, steep rock rising above a deep ravine.

His eldest son, Dimitris, had been in love with this place since childhood. Even then, he understood that it was one of the most beautiful spots in the village.

In the mornings, he would sit on the rock and watch the sunrise. His gaze travelled across the entire meadow and reached the lush green mountains surrounding it. All around him stretched the beauty of Mediterranean nature: olive trees, fig trees, mulberry trees, cypresses and prickly pears.

In winter, he remembers, the meadow would fill with water, and his father's piece of land would be transformed into a privileged balcony overlooking an endless silver lake.

Each side of the plot opened onto a different part of village life.

To the south stands the village primary school, a neoclassical building dating from 1910 — one of the island's most distinctive buildings and an authentic example of Greek Neoclassicism, from a period when the neoclassical tradition was, in a sense, returning to its birthplace.

To the west lies the traditional village park, where generations of children have played, run and laughed. Within the park stands the Orthodox Church of Agia Thekli, an authentic example of village architecture: simple, modest and deeply human.

To the north, the roads lead towards Corfu Town and the many beautiful traditional villages of the surrounding area.

Today, The Olive Tree House stands on that same rock. It looks east, towards the meadow that has always remained there — the first light of the day, the open view and the sense of freedom that accompanied Dimitris throughout his childhood.

The land beneath the house is not simply a plot. It is a place of observation, memory and return — a place that was loved long before the house was built, that continues to preserve our family's history, and that now becomes part of the memories of those who stay here.

For years the house belonged to the family's own summers. As a young adult, Lamprini spent every season here — university holidays, then time away from work — and filled it with friends from across Greece and beyond, drawn to Corfu. In those years it was mostly somewhere to rest between adventures — long days of swimming and watersports, and Corfu Town well after midnight, where the night has its own rhythm. Later it became somewhere to slow down and unwind; later still, a place to cook and gather friends around a table.

The house has held all of these summers. It has always known how to suit whoever it is looking after — which is, perhaps, the best thing a house can learn before it opens its doors to guests.

Your stories

"We woke each morning to the sound of birds, and coffee overlooking the meadow became our little ritual. The house sits in a wonderfully quiet spot, yet the village square is just a short walk away. We very much loved the authentic atmosphere of Liapades, the local fish (definitely try the marinated gavros) and Corfiot dishes, and the local wine. One afternoon the owners' parents, who live nearby, brought us fresh figs from a friend's land and loukoumades still warm from the pan (the kind of welcome you can't book). We had peaceful mornings and warm evenings; exactly what we were hoping for."

— Laurent T., France, 2025 · (Couple)

"A wonderfully comfortable stay for our family. Our two children loved having their own bedroom, and the house was full of thoughtful touches that made travelling with children so much easier, from board games to beach essentials. The village was just a short walk away, so everything felt effortless. One afternoon I filmed the children playing board games on the balcony, surrounded by greenery with the sound of the cicadas in the background. It is a little video of our Corfiot summer that we will treasure, and one they will enjoy looking back on when they are older. A beautifully designed house for families."

— Charlotte B., England, 2024 · (Family)

"The house matched the description exactly, everything was clean, well-organised and as stated. The kitchen is well equipped, the room-darkening blinds made for peaceful day naps, and the arrival information was clear and accurate. A quiet, reliable place for a family stay."

— Johannes K., Germany, 2021 · (Family)

"By the second morning we had a routine: espresso first, then deciding what the day would be. Some days it was Corfu Town, close enough for a coffee, some sightseeing or dinner. Other days we didn't go further than the village, wandering its little streets, which we loved most at night. But every evening ended the same way, on the west balcony, watching the sun go down. The house has real character; by the time we left, it felt like ours."

— Giulia R., Italy, 2018 · (Couple)

"I stayed for a longer stretch over winter, working remotely, and the house was genuinely comfortable for it. The Wi-Fi is fast, the heating works well, and the kitchen and washing machine made everyday life easy. The winter landscape is something else. I especially loved the wet meadow after the thunderstorms. Great location."

— Daniel M., USA, 2014 · (Solo traveller)
